To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pulmonary interstitial infiltration of eosinophilic granulocytes in rats infected with the canine round worm Toxocara (sic) canis (T. canis) causes airway and vascular smooth muscle remodeling, increases the baseline resistance of airways and small vessels, increases the reactivity of airways and blood vessels to the muscarinic agonist, acetylcholine, and decreases the reactivity of small vessels to isoproterenol.
pulmonary infiltration of eosinhophils without exogeneous activators caused airway and vascular remodelling and increased muscarinic reactivity in rat lungs infected by Toxocara canis.

pulmonary infiltration of eosinsophils causes airway and vascular smooth muscle thickening, and increases airway and vascular resistance, and increases airways and vascular reactivity to acetylcholine in rat lungs infected by T. canis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of eosinophis in the pathophysiology of airway and vascular disease in asthma.
the effects of pulmonary interstitial infiltration of eosinophil granulocytes on airways and vessels and their response to acetylcholine.
the mechanisms by which eosinophils contribute to the pathophysiology of allergic airways and vascular diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the eosinophils are the primary cause of the vascular and airway hyperresponsiveness in T. canis infected rats.

the eosinophils in this model of pulmonary eosinophilia are not activated by exogenous stimuli but are capable of producing significant vascular and airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling in the rat lung.
eosinophils can induce airway and vascular changes and hyperreactivity in the lungs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
eosinophils are the primary effector cells in allergic inflammation and that they cause airway and pulmonary vascular hyperresponsiveness and remodeling.
eosinophil-induced vascular and airways remodeling is associated with increased vascular permeability and increased muscarinic reactivity in rat lungs infected by T. canis.
eosinophilia causes vascular and airway hyperresponsiveness and remodeling in rat lungs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
eosinophils play an important role in remodeling and hyperresponsivity of the lung.
the eosinophil is the primary cell that is responsible for airway remodeling and vascular remodeling in this model.
the presence of eosinophila in the lung can cause vascular and airway hyperreactivity.
